source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 3 (PDF 37-48, printed 33-44); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 3 (Object Oriented Programming Using Python), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 According to the chapter introduction, polymorphism is studied in order to create:
blocks.explanation: The introduction says students study polymorphism to create flexible, adaptable programs.

book_ref.quote: Students will also study polymorphism to create flexible, adaptable programs.

blocks.prompt: 2 Object-Oriented Programming is a method of designing programs using:
blocks.explanation: OOP is a method of designing programs using objects and classes.

book_ref.quote: Object-Oriented Programming is a method of designing programs using objects and classes.

blocks.prompt: 3 In OOP, each object represents:

options.text: a real-world entity with specific properties and behaviors

blocks.explanation: Each object represents a real-world entity with specific properties and behaviors.

book_ref.quote: Each object represents a real-world entity with specific properties and behaviors.

blocks.prompt: 4 Which of the following acts as a template for creating many objects with similar characteristics?
blocks.explanation: Classes act as templates for creating multiple objects with similar characteristics.

book_ref.quote: Classes act as templates for creating multiple objects with similar characteristics.

blocks.prompt: 5 Which of the following is NOT one of the three ideas OOP emphasizes to manage data and behavior?
blocks.explanation: OOP emphasizes encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism to manage data and behavior efficiently.

book_ref.quote: OOP emphasizes encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism to manage data and behavior efficiently.

blocks.prompt: 6 The benefit of OOP by which code is divided into modules so that it is easier to manage is:
blocks.explanation: OOP allows code to be divided into modules, making it easier to manage; this is modularity.

book_ref.quote: OOP allows code to be divided into modules, making it easier to manage.

blocks.prompt: 7 Using the same classes and objects in several programs, so that repetition is reduced, is called:
blocks.explanation: Classes and objects can be reused in multiple programs or parts of a program, reducing repetition (reusability).

book_ref.quote: Classes and objects can be reused in multiple programs or parts of a program, reducing repetition.

blocks.prompt: 8 Programs built with OOP are easier to maintain and update because:

options.text: a change in one part does not affect the entire system
every change rewrites the whole program

blocks.explanation: OOP programs are easier to maintain and update because changes in one part do not affect the entire system.

book_ref.quote: because changes in one part do not affect the entire system

blocks.prompt: 9 The structure of OOP supports which two qualities in software development?
blocks.explanation: The structure of OOP supports scalability and adaptability in software development.

book_ref.quote: The structure of OOP supports scalability and adaptability in software development.

blocks.prompt: 10 OOP improves collaboration among programmers by:

options.text: hiding all code from the team
making code more understandable and organized
making every program one long block

blocks.explanation: OOP improves collaboration by making code more understandable and organized.

book_ref.quote: It also improves collaboration by making code more understandable and organized.

blocks.prompt: 11 According to the Tidbit, OOP helps programmers think in terms of:

options.text: real-life objects, like students or cars

blocks.explanation: The Tidbit: OOP helps programmers think in terms of real-life objects, like students or cars, making programs easier to understand.

book_ref.quote: Object-Oriented Programming helps programmers think in terms of real-life objects, like students or cars

blocks.prompt: 12 Modularity means:

options.text: writing the whole program in one function
copying the same code many times
dividing a program into smaller parts that can be developed and maintained separately

blocks.explanation: The Summary: modularity means dividing a program into smaller, manageable parts so each part can be developed and maintained separately.

book_ref.quote: Modularity means dividing a program into smaller, manageable parts so that each part can be developed and maintained separately.

blocks.prompt: 13 Which of the following is NOT a core concept of OOP named in Section 3.2?
blocks.explanation: The core concepts are classes and objects, encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism.

book_ref.quote: These concepts include classes and objects, encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism.

blocks.prompt: 14 If the map (blueprint) of a house is a class, then a house actually built from that map is:
blocks.explanation: A class is like a blueprint, while an object is the real thing created from that blueprint.

book_ref.quote: A class is like a blueprint, while an object is the real thing created from that blueprint.

blocks.prompt: 15 In a class, the actions of an entity are written as:
blocks.explanation: A class defines the properties (attributes) and actions (methods) of an entity.

book_ref.quote: A class is a blueprint or template that defines the properties (attributes) and actions (methods) of an entity.

blocks.prompt: 16 In a class, the properties of an entity are also called:
blocks.explanation: A class defines the properties (attributes) and actions (methods) of an entity.

book_ref.quote: A class is a blueprint or template that defines the properties (attributes) and actions (methods) of an entity.

blocks.prompt: 17 An instance of a class that holds actual values for its attributes is called:
blocks.explanation: An object is an instance of a class that holds actual values for its attributes.

book_ref.quote: An object is an instance of a class that holds actual values for its attributes

blocks.prompt: 18 In the book's Student class, which method sets the name automatically when an object is created?
blocks.explanation: In the Student example, __init__ sets the name when an object is created; display() prints it.

book_ref.quote: __init__ → sets the name when an object is created

blocks.explanation: Each object has its own data. info() is called on b2, so it prints b2's title and pages separated by a space.

book_ref.quote: Each object has its own data (Ali, Ahmed)

blocks.prompt:
20 What is the output of the following program?

class Counter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.count = 0

    def add(self):
        self.count += 1

c1 = Counter()
c2 = Counter()
c1.add()
c1.add()
c2.add()
print(c1.count, c2.count)
blocks.explanation: c1 and c2 are separate objects, each with its own count. add() is called twice on c1 and once on c2.

book_ref.quote: Using classes and objects helps organize data and related functionality together, making programs more structured.

blocks.prompt: 21 Inside an instance method, the parameter self refers to:

options.text: the last object created in the program

blocks.explanation: self is the reference to the current object, passed automatically to instance methods.

book_ref.quote: self is the reference to the current object, passed automatically to instance methods.

blocks.prompt: 22 In encapsulation, data and methods are bundled into a single unit called a:
blocks.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data (variables) and methods (functions) into a single unit (class) and restricts direct access to the data.

book_ref.quote: bundle data (variables) and methods (functions) into a single unit (class) and restrict direct access to the data

blocks.prompt: 23 Unlike Java or C++, Python signals how class data should be accessed by using:
blocks.explanation: Python does not have strict private or protected keywords; it relies on naming conventions to signal how data should be accessed.

book_ref.quote: Unlike languages like Java or C++, Python does not have strict

blocks.prompt: 24 According to the Tidbit on encapsulation, data should be:

options.text: hidden, with access controlled using methods

blocks.explanation: The Tidbit: hide the data and control access using methods.

book_ref.quote: Hide the data and control access using methods.

blocks.prompt: 25 Which of the following is NOT a reason why encapsulation is important?

options.text: It protects data from unwanted access
It lets any code change the data directly

blocks.explanation: Encapsulation protects data from unwanted access, improves security, makes code easier to manage and allows controlled modification; it stops direct changes.

book_ref.quote: Protects data from unwanted access

blocks.prompt: 26 In the chapter's bank-account example of encapsulation, the hidden balance can be used only through:
blocks.explanation: Your balance is hidden; you can only access it using deposit() and withdraw(). You cannot directly change it; this is encapsulation.

book_ref.quote: You cannot directly change the balance; this is encapsulation.

blocks.prompt: 27 If no underscore is used, a member such as self.name in a Python class is:
blocks.explanation: Public members are accessible from anywhere; by default all members in Python are public (syntax self.attribute_name).

book_ref.quote: By default, all members in Python are public

blocks.prompt: 28 An attribute written as self._marks (one underscore) is a:
blocks.explanation: A single underscore, self._attribute_name, marks a protected member meant for use within the class and its subclasses.

book_ref.quote: Syntax: self._attribute_name (single underscore)

blocks.prompt: 29 An attribute written as self.__pin (two underscores) is a:
blocks.explanation: A double underscore, self.__attribute_name, marks a private member that cannot be easily accessed from outside the class.

book_ref.quote: Syntax: self.__attribute_name (double underscore)

blocks.prompt: 30 The mechanism Python uses to change the internal name of a private variable to prevent accidental access is called:
blocks.explanation: Python uses a mechanism called name mangling to change the internal name of a private variable to prevent accidental access.

book_ref.quote: Python uses a mechanism called Name Mangling to change the internal name of the variable to prevent accidental access.

blocks.prompt: 31 A protected member (single underscore) in Python is:

options.text: a strict restriction enforced by Python
the same as a private member

blocks.explanation: A protected member is a convention (not a restriction) that tells other developers not to access it from outside.

book_ref.quote: It is a convention (not a restriction) to signal to other developers that the member should not be accessed from outside.

blocks.prompt: 32 Which variable name correctly marks a private variable in Python?
blocks.explanation: A private member has two underscores, __private_variable. One underscore (_private_variable) marks a protected member (book correction to Figure 3.2).

book_ref.quote: a private member has two underscores

blocks.explanation: 800 - 300 leaves 500. The second spend(600) is more than 500, so it prints Not enough money and the balance stays 500.

book_ref.quote: These are highly restricted and cannot be easily accessed from outside the class.

blocks.explanation: __amount is private; name mangling changes its internal name, so direct access from outside the class fails with AttributeError.

book_ref.quote: Python uses a mechanism called Name Mangling to change the internal name of the variable to prevent accidental access.

blocks.explanation: _marks is protected only by convention (not a restriction), so Python still allows the access and prints the value.

book_ref.quote: These are intended for internal use within the class and its subclasses.

blocks.prompt: 36 In inheritance, the new class that takes properties and methods from another class is called a:
blocks.explanation: The new class, called a subclass, can add or modify features of the parent class.

book_ref.quote: The new class, called a subclass, can add or modify features of the parent class.

blocks.prompt: 37 Inheritance promotes code reuse and reduces:
blocks.explanation: Inheritance promotes code reuse and reduces redundancy (repeated code).

book_ref.quote: Inheritance promotes code reuse and reduces redundancy.

blocks.prompt: 38 With inheritance, a program can be extended:

options.text: only by deleting the parent class
only by copying the whole parent class

blocks.explanation: Inheritance makes it easier to extend programs without rewriting existing code.

book_ref.quote: It also makes it easier to extend programs without rewriting existing code.

blocks.prompt: 39 When a child class inherits from exactly one parent class, it is called:
blocks.explanation: Single inheritance occurs when a child class inherits attributes and methods from exactly one parent class.

book_ref.quote: Single inheritance occurs when a child class (subclass) inherits attributes and methods from exactly one parent class (superclass).

blocks.prompt: 40 The most fundamental form of inheritance in Python is:
blocks.explanation: Single inheritance is the most fundamental form of inheritance in Python.

book_ref.quote: This is the most fundamental form of inheritance in Python

blocks.prompt: 41 Which header correctly defines a class Car that inherits from Vehicle?
blocks.explanation: A child class is defined by passing the parent class name in parentheses: class Child(Parent):.

book_ref.quote: It is defined by passing the parent class name in parentheses

blocks.prompt: 42 The class whose properties are inherited is also called the:
blocks.explanation: Parent Class (Base Class) is the class whose properties are inherited; the child class is the derived class.

book_ref.quote: Parent Class (Base Class): The class whose properties are inherited.

blocks.prompt: 43 Inside an overriding method, the parent's version of the same method can be called with:
blocks.explanation: A child class can override a parent method; you can use the super() function to call the parent's version of that method.

book_ref.quote: You can use the super() function to call the parent

blocks.explanation: Teacher inherits __init__ and greet() from Person and adds teach(). print() with commas puts one space between items.

book_ref.quote: In this example, the Dog class inherits the basic functionality of an Animal but adds its own specific behavior.

blocks.explanation: The child (Dog) inherits from the parent (Animal), not the other way round. An Animal object has no bark() method, so AttributeError occurs.

book_ref.quote: The class that inherits from the parent.

blocks.prompt: 46 A Smartphone class that inherits from both a Camera class and a Computer class is an example of:
blocks.explanation: Multiple inheritance lets a single class inherit from more than one parent class, such as a Smartphone inheriting from Camera and Computer.

book_ref.quote: such as a Smartphone class inheriting from both a Camera and a Computer class

blocks.explanation: Artist inherits from both Writer and Singer, so it has sing() and write() as well as its own paint(). The methods run in the order they are called.

book_ref.quote: This enables a child class to combine behaviors from different sources

blocks.prompt: 48 A chain of inheritance like Grandparent → Parent → Child is called:
blocks.explanation: Multilevel inheritance occurs when a class inherits from another derived class, creating a chain like a family tree.

book_ref.quote: creating a chain of inheritance similar to a family tree (Grandparent → Parent → Child)

blocks.prompt: 49 In multilevel inheritance, the grandchild class has access to the methods and attributes of:

options.text: both its parent and its grandparent

blocks.explanation: The grandchild class has access to all methods and attributes from both its immediate parent and its grandparent.

book_ref.quote: class has access to all methods and attributes from both its immediate parent and its grandparent

blocks.prompt: 50 In the book's example, ElectricCar inherits from Car, and Car inherits from Vehicle. The method start_engine() used by an ElectricCar object is defined in:
blocks.explanation: start_engine() is defined in the base class Vehicle and reaches ElectricCar through Car; drive() is in Car and charge() in ElectricCar.

book_ref.quote: In this example, ElectricCar inherits from Car, which in turn inherits from Vehicle.

blocks.explanation: SmartPhone inherits from Phone, which inherits from Device, so x can use browse() and also power_on() from the grandparent.

book_ref.quote: Multilevel inheritance in Python occurs when a class inherits from another drived class

blocks.prompt: 52 The word polymorphism means:
blocks.explanation: Polymorphism means many forms: the ability of an entity (like a function or object) to perform different actions based on the context.

book_ref.quote: It refers to the ability of an entity (like a function or object) to perform different actions based on the context.

blocks.prompt: 53 Technically, polymorphism allows the same method, function or operator to:

options.text: behave differently depending on the object it is working with
run only once in a program

blocks.explanation: Polymorphism allows the same method, function or operator to behave differently depending on the object it is working with.

book_ref.quote: allows the same method, function, or operator to behave differently depending on the object it is working with

blocks.prompt: 54 In the chapter's payment-system example, all payment types use processPayment(). For NetBanking this method:
blocks.explanation: All payment types use the common method processPayment() with different implementations; for NetBanking it redirects to bank login. The name stays the same, the action changes.

book_ref.quote: NetBanking Payment: redirects to bank login

blocks.prompt:
55 What is the output of the following program?

print(3 + 4, "3" + "4")
blocks.explanation: The same + operator behaves differently with different objects: it adds two numbers (7) but joins two strings ("34").

book_ref.quote: Technically, Polymorphism allows the same method, function, or operator to behave differently

blocks.prompt: 56 The two main types of polymorphism are:
blocks.explanation: Polymorphism mainly includes compile-time and runtime polymorphism.

book_ref.quote: It mainly includes compile-time and runtime polymorphism

blocks.prompt: 57 Compile-time polymorphism is usually achieved through:
blocks.explanation: Compile-time polymorphism decides which method or operation to run during compilation, usually through method or operator overloading.

book_ref.quote: usually through method or operator overloading

blocks.prompt: 58 Which statement about Python is correct?

options.text: Python supports overloading exactly like Java
Python does not allow default arguments
Python cannot accept arguments of different types
Python does not support true method overloading based on function signatures

blocks.explanation: Unlike Java or C++, Python does not support true method overloading based on function signatures.

book_ref.quote: But python does not support true method overloading based on function signatures

blocks.prompt: 59 Signature-based overloading is unnecessary in Python mainly because:

options.text: Python is dynamically typed, so one function can accept arguments of different types

blocks.explanation: Because Python is dynamically typed, a single function can accept arguments of different types, making signature-based overloading unnecessary.

book_ref.quote: Because Python is dynamically typed, a single function can accept arguments of different types

blocks.prompt: 60 Which of the following is NOT a way given in the chapter to get overloading-like behavior in Python?

options.text: Writing two methods with the same name and different parameter lists

blocks.explanation: Similar behavior is achieved using default arguments, variable-length arguments (*args, **kwargs) or conditional logic inside the function, not by true signature-based overloading.

book_ref.quote: Instead, similar behavior can be achieved using default arguments, variable-length arguments (*args, **kwargs), or conditional logic inside the function.

blocks.explanation: add(5) uses b = 0, giving 5. add(2, 3, 4, 1) puts 4 and 1 in *args: 2 + 3 + 4 + 1 = 10. One method works with different numbers of inputs.

book_ref.quote: The multiply() method works with different numbers of inputs, mimicking compile-time polymorphism.

blocks.explanation: With no arguments, the defaults a = 0 and b = 0 are used and *args is empty, so the method returns 0.

book_ref.quote: This code demonstrates method overloading using default and variable-length arguments.

blocks.prompt: 63 Runtime polymorphism happens through:
blocks.explanation: Runtime polymorphism happens through method overriding: a child class provides its own version of a method already defined in the parent class.

book_ref.quote: This happens through Method Overriding a child class provides its own version of a method already defined in the parent class.

blocks.prompt: 64 In runtime polymorphism, which version of a method runs is decided:

options.text: only by the programmer by hand
by the name of the file
while the program is running, based on the object calling it

blocks.explanation: Runtime polymorphism means the behavior of a method is decided while the program is running, based on the object calling it.

book_ref.quote: Runtime polymorphism means that the behavior of a method is decided while program is running, based on the object calling it.

blocks.explanation: area() is overridden in Square (3 x 3 = 9) and Rectangle (2 x 5 = 10); Shape keeps its own version (0). The right method is chosen at runtime by each object's class.

book_ref.quote: At runtime, the correct method is called based on object

blocks.explanation: Cow overrides sound(); inside it, super().sound() first calls the parent's version (Some sound) and then Moo is printed.

book_ref.quote: Method Overriding: A child class can provide a specific implementation of a method that is already provided by its parent.

blocks.prompt: 67 Using the same method or operation in different ways depending on the object is called:
blocks.explanation: The Summary: polymorphism means using the same method or operation in different ways depending on the object; it makes code flexible and adaptable.

book_ref.quote: Polymorphism means using the same method or operation in different ways depending on the object.
